lemma: Restriction lemma (exact). Let g(x) = [w.x >= t] on {0,1}^n with integer weights w, S+(F) = sum_{i in F, w_i>0} w_i, S-(F) = sum_{i in F, w_i<0} w_i, for a free set F. Fix the other variables by rho in {0,1}^{[n]\F}, and set c = sum_{i not in F} w_i rho_i. Then g restricted by rho is non-constant iff S-(F) < t - c <= S+(F). Proof: on the free cube, w.x restricted equals c + sum_{i in F} w_i x_i, a linear function whose minimum and maximum over {0,1}^F are attained at the vertices x_i = [w_i<0] and x_i = [w_i>0], with values c+S-(F) and c+S+(F). g is constant 1 iff min >= t, constant 0 iff max < t, so non-constant iff min < t <= max. Consequence: a restriction shifts every threshold by c and shrinks the window to width W_F = sum_{i in F} |w_i|; a bottom gate survives the restriction iff its shifted threshold lies in the window.

lemma: Restriction lemma for bottom THR gates (Erdos-Littlewood-Offord form): for integer weights |w_j| <= B, a set R of r variables, and x_F uniform on the rest, P(gate undecided) <= min(1, sum_{j in R}|w_j| / sqrt(N_F)) <= rB / sqrt(N_F), where N_F = #{j in F: w_j != 0}. In particular the undecided fraction is O(rB/sqrt(n)) when N_F >= n/2, so it tends to 0 for r = o(sqrt n). The regime r ~ sqrt(n)/B is the threshold where the bound stops being useful.
proved_step: LEMMA (anti-concentration over subset sums). Let a_1..a_N be nonzero integers, x_j iid uniform in {0,1}, c = sum a_j x_j. For integers a and L >= 0: P(c in {a,...,a+L-1}) <= L*C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= L/sqrt(N). PROOF: Erdos (1945): for reals |a_j|>=1, any open interval J of length 1 contains the subset sums of at most C(N,floor(N/2)) subsets. Each integer v lies in the open interval (v-1/2, v+1/2), so #{S : c_S = v} <= C(N,floor(N/2)); sum over the L integers and divide by 2^N. For the second inequality use C(2k,k) <= 4^k/sqrt(pi k): if N=2k then pi k = pi N/2 >= N; if N=2k+1 then C(2k+1,k) = C(2k+2,k+1)/2 <= 4^{k+1}/(2 sqrt(pi(k+1))), so the ratio is <= 1/sqrt(pi(k+1)) <= 1/sqrt(2k+1). COROLLARY (bottom gate). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integers |w_j| <= B, R a set of r variables, F the rest, c = sum_{j in F} w_j x_j. Put lo = sum_{j in R} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in R} max(w_j,0). Then g is decided under the restriction (constant over all completions of x_R) iff c >= t-lo or c < t-hi. So g is undecided iff t-hi <= c < t-lo, an integer window of exactly L = hi-lo = sum_{j in R}|w_j| <= rB integers. Applying the lemma with N = N_F gives P_{x_F}(undecided) <= min(1, rB/sqrt(N_F)). Summing over the m bottom gates gives E[#undecided] <= sum_g min(1, rB/sqrt(N_F(g))). SCOPE / WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the bound is worst-case over weights with |w|<=B and integer; it needs many nonzero free weights (N_F large) and says nothing for sparse gates; it bounds only the bottom layer; no running time follows yet (the top gate is not handled). KNOWLEDGE vs ALGORITHMIC: knowledge = the restriction bound with its threshold r ~ sqrt(n)/B (explains the refuted fixed-p experiments: for r = pn the bound is ~pB sqrt(n) >= 1); algorithmic gain = none yet. NOVELTY: the Erdos theorem is classical; the new content is the application to restricted THR gates and the regime boundary. The exact per-gate check is run in the next computation.

lemma: Theorem C (bounded-weight switching bound for one bottom THR gate). Setting: g(x)=[sum_i w_i x_i >= t] on {0,1}^n, integer weights, nz = number of nonzero weights, M = max|w_i| >= 1. Random restriction R_p: each variable free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Claim: for 0 < p <= 1/4, P(restricted g is non-constant) <= exp(-p nz/3) + 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Corollary: p = 1/(16 M sqrt(nz)) with sqrt(nz) >= 126 M gives P(non-constant) <= 1/4. Proof: Lemma A (Sperner): for nonzero integers a_1..a_k and uniform eps in {0,1}^k, P(sum a_i eps_i = v) <= C(k, floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k) for every v (flip eps_i where a_i<0; the sets with a given sum form an antichain). Lemma B: given the free set F, the non-constancy window of the restriction lemma has W_F integers, so P(non-constant | F) <= W_F/sqrt(k) <= M s/sqrt(k), with s = number of free nonzero-weight variables and k = nz - s >= 1. Chernoff: P(s > 2 p nz) <= exp(-p nz/3). On s <= 2 p nz (and p <= 1/4) we have k >= nz/2, giving conditional bound 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Take the expectation over s.

proved_step:
LEMMA (Exact undecided probability under random restriction with uniform threshold). Let g(x) = [∑_{i=1}^n w_i x_i ≥ t] be a threshold gate with integer weights w_i, S = ∑ |w_i|. Let R_p be the random restriction: each variable is free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Let the threshold t be chosen uniformly from {t_min, ..., t_max} where the interval length L = t_max - t_min + 1 satisfies L ≥ S (in particular, t uniform on [-S, S] works). Then P_{R_p, t}[g|R_p is non-constant] ≤ p, with equality when L = S and the threshold range matches the possible sums exactly.

PROOF. For a fixed restriction ρ, let F be the set of free variables. The restricted gate is g_ρ(y) = [∑_{i∈F} w_i y_i ≥ t - ∑_{i∉F} w_i ρ(i)]. This is non-constant iff the threshold t falls in the interval I_ρ = (L_ρ, U_ρ] where L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i<0} w_i, U_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i>0} w_i. The length of I_ρ is U_ρ - L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F} |w_i| =: W_F. Since t is uniform over an interval of length L ≥ S ≥ W_F, P_t[g_ρ non-constant] = W_F / L ≤ W_F / S. Now take expectation over R_p: E[W_F] = ∑_i |w_i| · P(i free) = p S. Thus P_{R_p,t}[undecided] = E[W_F/L] ≤ E[W_F/S] = p. Equality holds when L = S and the threshold distribution is uniform over exactly S+1 consecutive integers covering the full range of possible sums. ∎

lemma: Lemma R1 (Kolmogorov-Rogozin reduction, unbounded weights). Let a_1..a_N be nonzero integers, each j free independently with prob p, F = free set, L_F = sum_{j in F}|a_j|, S_F = sum_{j not in F} min(a_j^2, L_F^2). Then P(gate nonconstant) <= sqrt(8) * A * E_F[min(1, L_F / sqrt(S_F))], where A is the universal Kolmogorov-Rogozin constant. Proof: condition on F. Nonconstancy means X = sum_{j not in F} a_j u_j (u_j iid uniform bits) lies in a window of exactly L_F consecutive integers. Apply Rogozin with L = L_F and L_j = min(|a_j|/2, L). Each X_j = a_j u_j has Q_j(L_j) <= 1/2, since an interval of length < |a_j| contains at most one of {0, a_j}. Hence sum L_j^2 (1 - Q_j) >= (1/8) S_F, which gives the bound.

lemma: Lemma (sparse-restriction bound, one THR gate). Let g(x) = [Σ_j w_j x_j ≥ t] with integer weights, nz = #{j : w_j ≠ 0} ≥ 2. Choose a uniform k-subset F of variables, with 1 ≤ k ≤ nz/2, and fix the variables outside F to uniform bits. Then P[g restricted is non-constant] ≤ k · ((1/n) Σ_j |w_j|) · √(2/nz). Proof: Let lo = Σ_{j∈F} min(w_j,0), hi = Σ_{j∈F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi−lo (window width). The restriction is non-constant iff t−hi ≤ c < t−lo where c = Σ_{j∉F} w_j x_j. Given free set F of size k, there are r = #{j∉F : w_j≠0} ≥ nz−k ≥ nz/2 free nonzero weights. Flipping bits where w_j<0 turns c into a sum of r positive integers; sets with fixed sum form an antichain, so by Sperner P[c=v] ≤ C(r,⌊r/2⌋)/2^r ≤ 1/√r for every v. Hence P[non-constant|F] ≤ W_F/√r ≤ W_F·√(2/nz). Since P[j∈F]=k/n, E[W_F]=(k/n)Σ_j|w_j|. Taking expectation over F gives the claim. Consequence: for k=O(1) the undecided fraction is O(k·mean|w|/√n), giving the 1/√n decay; for k=c√n it gives only order c·mean|w|, consistent with measured Θ(1).

proved_step: Lemma (heavy-split restriction bound, repair of G0008). Setting: g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t], integer weights w_j, any integer t, n variables, nz = #{j : w_j != 0}. Fix tau >= 1 and H = #{j : |w_j| > tau}. Let F be a uniform k-subset of variables, 1 <= k <= nz/2, and fix the other variables to uniform bits. Then P[restriction of g is non-constant] <= k*H/n + A*(tau*k + 1)*sqrt(2/(nz - k)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality (cited; exact constant and statement to be source-checked). Proof: (1) Let E = {F contains a heavy variable}. P(E) <= E[#heavy in F] = k*H/n by a union bound. (2) On the complement of E, every j in F has |w_j| <= tau, so W_F := sum_{j in F} |w_j| <= tau*k. (3) Given F, the restriction is non-constant iff c := sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in the integer window [t - hi, t - lo), where hi, lo are the positive and negative parts summed over F; this window has W_F integer points. (4) Let r = #{j not in F : w_j != 0} >= nz - k. Each summand w_j x_j takes values 0 and w_j, so its sup-probability on any half-open integer interval of length 1 is at most 1/2. Kolmogorov-Rogozin with scales l_j = 1 gives sup_x P(c in [x, x+L)) <= A*L/sqrt(r/2) for L >= 1; with L = W_F + 1 this is <= A*(W_F+1)*sqrt(2/r) <= A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)) on the complement of E. (5) Combine: P(nonconst) <= P(E) + sup over the complement = k*H/n + A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)). QED (modulo source-check of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin statement). The bound does not depend on the maximum weight M.

proved_step: Lemma (exact unit-weight average, lane C). Let g(x) = [x_1 + ... + x_n >= t] with all weights 1. Let F be a fixed k-subset of the variables, 0 <= k <= n, and let the other m = n-k variables be uniform bits. Let t be uniform on the 2n+1 integers -n..n. Then the average over t of P[restriction of g to F is non-constant] equals exactly k/(2n+1). Proof: let c = sum of the m free bits, so 0 <= c <= m. Let s = number of ones in F, 0 <= s <= k. The restriction is non-constant iff c < t <= c+k, i.e. c in [t-k, t-1]. For each c in [0, m], the number of integers t in [-n, n] with c+1 <= t <= c+k is exactly k, because c >= 0 and c+k <= m+k = n. Summing over t and averaging over c gives k/(2n+1). QED. Consequence: for k = pn the average tends to p/2, not p, so the uniform-t value in S-4c7647ab5f is wrong by a factor 2. The lemma is an identity, not a bound. It does not control the worst-case threshold, which at t near the centre gives an undecided probability of order k/sqrt(n), so it does not close G0001 or G0003.

proved_step: LEMMA R (window bound, arbitrary integer weights, uniform in the threshold). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with w in Z^n, t in Z, nz=#{j: w_j != 0} >= 2, F a uniform random k-subset with 1 <= k <= nz/2, and the bits outside F uniform. Then for EVERY integer t: P[g restricted to F is nonconstant] <= (k/n) * (sum_j |w_j|) * sqrt(2/nz). PROOF. (1) Fix F. Put lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi - lo = sum_{j in F}|w_j|, and c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j. The restriction is nonconstant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, i.e. c lies in a window of exactly W_F consecutive integers. (2) Let r = #{j not in F: w_j != 0} >= nz - k >= nz/2. Replace x_j by 1 - x_j for each j not in F with w_j < 0 (a bijection of bit strings). Then c becomes sum_J a_j y_j over r indices with a_j = |w_j| > 0. For each fixed value v, the sets J with sum_{j in J} a_j = v form an antichain (A strictly inside B forces a strictly smaller sum), so by Sperner P[c = v | F] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r). (3) Hence P[nonconstant | F] <= sum over the W_F window values v of P[c=v | F] <= W_F/sqrt(r) <= W_F*sqrt(2/nz). (4) P[j in F] = k/n gives E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_j |w_j|. Taking the expectation over F proves the claim. QED. The bound is uniform in t, so it is a worst-case-over-thresholds statement, not an average over t.

proved_step: LEMMA (gcd-refined window bound, one THR gate, per fixed free set). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F a set of variables, and out = complement of F. Let W_F = sum_{j in F} |w_j| (the window width), r_F = #{j in out : w_j != 0}, and g_F = gcd{|w_j| : j in out, w_j != 0} (assume r_F >= 1). Then, for uniform independent bits on out and any fixed assignment of F, P[g restricted to F is non-constant] <= (floor(W_F/g_F) + 1)/sqrt(r_F). PROOF. (i) Non-constancy: let lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0). The F-part of the sum takes its minimum lo and maximum hi, so the restriction is non-constant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, where c = sum_{j in out} w_j x_j. (ii) Sperner: write y_j = x_j if w_j > 0 and y_j = 1 - x_j if w_j < 0. Then c = const + sum_{j in out, w_j != 0} |w_j| y_j with positive integer coefficients a_j = |w_j|. For a fixed value v the set {S : sum_{j in S} a_j = v} is an antichain of subsets of the r_F free positions, so P[c = v] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) (the central-binomial inequality holds for every r >= 1). (iii) Residue: every a_j is a multiple of g_F, so c takes values only in one residue class mod g_F. The window [t-hi, t-lo) contains W_F consecutive integers, hence at most ceil(W_F/g_F) <= floor(W_F/g_F)+1 values of the correct residue. Summing (ii) over these values gives P[nonconst | F] <= (floor(W_F/g_F)+1)/sqrt(r_F). QED. Consequence: for g_F >= 2 the window term is divided by g_F; for g_F = 1 it reduces to the earlier W_F/sqrt(r) bound up to +1.

lemma: L2-window lemma (per gate, conditional on F). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F subset [n] fixed, x_F fixed, x_O uniform in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Let WF = sum_{j in F}|w_j| >= 1 and Neff(F) = sum_{j not in F, w_j != 0} min(|w_j|, WF)^2. Then P_{x_O}[g|F nonconstant] <= sqrt(2)*A*WF/sqrt(Neff(F)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality Q(S;L) <= A*L*(sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q(X_j;l_j)))^{-1/2} (0<l_j<=L). Proof: nonconstancy means the shift c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in a window of WF consecutive integers, so the probability is at most Q(c;WF). Take l_j = min(|w_j|, WF) <= WF. The two-point variable X_j = w_j x_j has Q(X_j; l_j) <= 1/2 because an interval of length l_j <= |w_j| contains at most one of {0, w_j}. So sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q_j) >= Neff/2 and the inequality gives the bound. The constant is scale-invariant in w.

PROOF. Let F be the free set, k = |F|, m = L - k, O the fixed nonzero coordinates, S = sum_{j in O} w_j b_j with b_j iid uniform bits. (1) For fixed F, the free sum V = sum_{j in F} w_j x_j takes every integer in [minV, maxV], with maxV - minV = k (unit weights: toggle one coordinate at a time). So g is nonconstant iff minV + S < t <= maxV + S, i.e. S lies in an integer interval of exactly k integers. (2) Writing -b_j = (1-b_j) - 1 for w_j = -1 gives S = Bin(m,1/2) + const, so max_a Pr[S=a] = q(m) := C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m. Hence Pr[nonconst | F] <= min(1, k q(m)). (3) q(m) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))) for m >= 2: for m = 2r, q = C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) (Wallis); for m = 2r+1, q(m) = q(2r)(2r+1)/(2r+2) <= q(2r). (4) If L >= 4 and k <= L/2 then m >= L/2 >= 2, m-1 >= L/4, so q(m) <= sqrt(8/(pi L)) <= 2/sqrt(L). (5) Average over k ~ Bin(L,p): E[min(1,k q(L-k)); k <= L/2] <= 2 E[k]/sqrt(L) = 2pL/sqrt(L) = 2p sqrt(L). The event k >= j, j = floor(L/2)+1 >= L/2, has probability <= C(L,j) p^j <= (eL/j)^j p^j <= (2ep)^j. Summing gives the claim. QED.

lemma: Exact window identity (unit weights, no probability). Let O be a set of N variables with weights w_j in {-1,+1}, N_+ positive and N_- negative. Its outside sum S(x_O) = sum_{j in O} w_j x_j takes exactly the integer values -N_- ... N_+, which are N+1 values. For a base b and threshold t, the gate g = [b + S >= t] is non-constant on {0,1}^O iff min S < t - b <= max S, i.e. iff t - b lies in {-N_- + 1, ..., N_+}. That set has exactly N integers. Proof: the extremes of S are attained at all-zero and all-one-on-the-matching-sign points, and S takes every intermediate integer because each unit step is one variable. Consequence: if P(t - b = v) <= q for every integer v, then P[g non-constant] <= N q. This is an exact identity, not a bound on the top gate, and it is trivial bookkeeping, so it does NOT count as progress and closes nothing.

lemma: Restriction lemma for integer weights (Lemma-B shape with explicit constant). Setting: integer weights w_j, t in Z, a set R of free variables with N=|R| and W_R = sum over R of |w_j|, F = complement of R, k = number of j in F with w_j != 0 (k >= 1), and x_F uniform in {0,1}^F. Claim: P_{x_F}[ g restricted to x_F is non-constant in x_R ] <= W_R * binom(k, floor(k/2)) / 2^k <= W_R / sqrt(k), where g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t]. For unit weights on all of [n] this reads N/sqrt(n-N). Proof. (1) Let S(x_R) = sum over R of w_j x_j, with max mx and min mn, so mx - mn = W_R. Put b = sum over F of w_j x_j. Then g is non-constant iff b + mn < t <= b + mx, i.e. iff t - b lies in the set of integers (mn, mx], which has exactly W_R elements and does not depend on x_F. (2) Write each fixed term w_j x_j = w_j/2 + a_j e_j with a_j = w_j/2 (|a_j| >= 1/2) and e_j = +-1 uniform. Erdos' 1945 Littlewood-Offord theorem (source-check needed) says that at most binom(k, floor(k/2)) of the 2^k sign vectors give a sum in any open interval of length 1 (after scaling by 2: |a'_j| >= 1 and length 2). A point lies in such an interval, so P[b = v] <= binom(k, floor(k/2))/2^k for every integer v. (3) P[nonconst] = P[t - b in (mn, mx]] <= sum over the W_R integers v of P[b = t - v] <= W_R * binom(k, floor(k/2))/2^k. (4) binom(k, floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k): for k = 2m or 2m+1 this follows from binom(2m,m)/4^m <= 1/sqrt(3m+1) (classical, by induction), since 3m+1 >= 2m. The case k = 1 gives 1/2 <= 1. QED.

lemma: Setting: m integer weight vectors W_j in Z^n, a fixed assignment rho on V minus F (|F| = k) with x_F free, and thresholds t_j drawn uniformly from {-R,...,R} independently of W and rho. Let mn_j = min over x_F of W_j.x and mx_j = max over x_F of W_j.x (both under rho). Gate j is undecided under rho iff mn_j < t_j <= mx_j. Then P_t[undecided] = |{integers in (mn_j, mx_j]} intersect [-R,R]| / (2R+1) <= sum_{i in F} |W_ji| / (2R+1). For W_ji uniform on {-B,...,B}: E|W_ji| = B(B+1)/(2B+1), so E[undecided fraction] <= k B(B+1)/((2B+1)(2R+1)). With R = B sqrt(n) this is about k/(4 sqrt n): the sparse restriction shrinks the undecided fraction only when k = o(sqrt n).

proved_step: LEMMA U (adversarial threshold, unit weights). Let n >= 2, p in (0,1), pn >= 2. Random restriction: each variable is free with probability p, otherwise fixed to 1 or to 0 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Single gate with w_i = 1 for all i and threshold t = ceil(n/2). Let a = number of variables fixed to 1, f = number free. The gate is undecided iff a < t <= a+f. Then P(undecided) >= 1 - 2*exp(-2*(pn/2 - 1)^2 / n). Proof: a is Bin(n, (1-p)/2) with mean (1-p)n/2; a >= t forces a - E[a] >= pn/2 - 1. a+f is Bin(n, (1+p)/2) with mean (1+p)n/2; a+f < t <= n/2 + 1/2 forces (E - value) >= pn/2 - 1. Hoeffding on each event gives the bound. Scope: one unit-weight gate, one threshold; it refutes the adversarial-threshold form of the p-bound (max_t P(undecided) <= p) for p >> 1/sqrt(n). It does not address random thresholds or general weights.

proved_step: LEMMA-C1 (disjoint-support subclass, exact counting). Let f(x) = [sum_{j=1}^m v_j [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, where the supports S_j are pairwise disjoint integer sets, |S_j| = k_j, w_j, t_j, v_j, T integers, V = sum_j |v_j|. Then #f = 2^{n - sum_j k_j} * sum over b in {0,1}^m with sum_j v_j b_j >= T of prod_j N_j(b_j), where N_j(b) = #{y in {0,1}^{S_j} : [w_j . y >= t_j] = b}. Proof: the blocks are disjoint, so the indicator variables [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] are independent over uniform x; the free variables outside the union of supports contribute 2^{n - sum k_j}. Running-time algorithm: a DP over j with state s in [-V, V] (partial sum of v_j b_j), computing N_j by enumerating 2^{k_j} points; time O(sum_j 2^{k_j} k_j + m (2V+1) + n). Hence for k_j <= c log n and V <= poly(n), #f is computed in poly(n) time, versus 2^n for brute force. Random restriction: free set F with |F| = f; each fixed variable is 1 with probability 1/2, independently. Single gate sum_i x_i >= t (all weights 1, any integer t). proved_step: LEMMA-C2 (bounded-overlap conditioning, exact). Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n with arbitrary integer supports S_j. Let occ(i) = #{j : i in S_j}, R = {i : occ(i) >= 2}, P_j = {i in S_j : occ(i) = 1}, free = #{i : occ(i) = 0}. Then #f = 2^{free} * sum over a in {0,1}^R of sum over b in {0,1}^m with sum_j v_j b_j >= T of prod_j N_j^a(b_j), where N_j^a(b) = #{y in {0,1}^{P_j} : [w_j . z = ... >= t_j] = b} with z the vector on S_j equal to a on S_j cap R and y on P_j. Proof: for fixed a, the indicator of block j is a function of y_{P_j} only; the sets P_j are pairwise disjoint, so the block indicators are independent under uniform y; summing over b with the threshold condition gives the formula, and summing over a and multiplying by 2^free gives #f. Running time: O(2^{|R|} (sum_j k_j 2^{|P_j|} + m (2V+1))) with V = sum_j |v_j|. proved_step: LEMMA-HUB (restricted class, exact counting). Setting: n variables; hub set R with |R| = k; the other variables are partitioned into disjoint blocks P_1..P_G. Every bottom gate j has support(W_j) contained in R union P_g(j) for one block g(j); J_g = {j : g(j) = g}. Weights v_j are integers with V = sum_j |v_j| bounded by a polynomial in n. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} = sum over h in {0,1}^k of sum over s >= T of (D_{1,h} * ... * D_{G,h})(s), where D_{g,h}(s) = #{y in {0,1}^{P_g} : sum_{j in J_g} v_j [W_j.(h,y) >= t_j] = s} and * is convolution of integer distributions. PROOF: fix h. The outcomes of the gates in J_g depend only on y_g, and the blocks use disjoint variables, so the block sums are independent over the product set {0,1}^{P_1} x ... x {0,1}^{P_G}; the number of product points with total sum >= T is the convolution formula. RUNNING TIME: computing D_{g,h} takes 2^{|P_g|} evaluations of the gates in J_g, each O(n); the convolutions over the range [-V, V] cost O(G V^2). Total 2^k (sum_g 2^{|P_g|} n m + G V^2) <= poly(n, m, V) * 2^{k + max_g |P_g|}. So if k + max_g |P_g| <= (1 - delta) n and V <= poly(n), #SAT is computed in time poly(n) * 2^{(1-delta) n}.

Random restriction: each variable is free (in F) independently with prob p; for i not in F the bit a_i is uniform in {0,1}, independent of F. For a FIXED integer t, let mn = sum_i min(0,w_i a_i) over i not in F plus sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), and mx analogously with max; gate undecided iff mn < t <= mx. Then P_{F,a}[undecided] <= 3*sqrt(2)*p*sqrt(n) (about 4.24 p sqrt n). PROOF. Fix F, let s=|F|, k=n-s. (1) mx-mn = s, so the set of values of base = sum_{i not in F} w_i a_i that make the gate undecided is a set of s consecutive integers. (2) Substitute b_i = 1-a_i for the k' indices with w_i=-1: base = sum_{w_i=+1} a_i + sum_{w_i=-1} b_i - const, a sum of k independent uniform bits plus a constant. (3) Sperner/Erdos: max_x P(Bin(k,1/2)=x) = C(k,floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k) for k>=1 (even k: C(2m,m)/4^m <= 1/sqrt(pi m) <= 1/sqrt(2m); odd k: the extra factor (2m+1)/(2m+2) <= 1 and 1/sqrt(pi m) <= 1/sqrt(2m+1) for m>=1; k=1 gives 1/2). Hence P(undecided | F) <= min(1, s/sqrt(k)) for k>=1, and <= 1 for k=0. (4) Average over F. Region A = {s <= n/2}: k >= n/2, so s/sqrt(k) <= s*sqrt(2/n); E[s] = pn gives contribution <= p*sqrt(2n). Region B = {s > n/2}: its probability is <= sum over |F|>=n/2 of p^{|F|} <= 2^n p^{n/2} = p * (2^n p^{n/2-1}) <= p * 2^n * 4^{-(n/2-1)} = 4p (using p<=1/4 and n/2-1>=0). Total <= p*sqrt(2n) + 4p = p*sqrt(n)*(sqrt(2)+4/sqrt(n)) <= 3*sqrt(2)*p*sqrt(n) for n>=2. QED. NOTE: the window bound is for an ADVERSARIAL fixed t; the uniform-t version (proof-state lemma above) is weaker and elementary. The random-a assumption is needed: the OR-gate example with all fixed bits 0 (exact, cm-33cf0317f7794fa7) has P/p ~ 0.79 sqrt(n) at p=1/n, which is consistent with the bound.

proved_step: CLAIMED S-R26-LEMMA-UNIFORM-THRESHOLD. Proof: fix F and a; let s = sum_{i notin F} w_i a_i, mn = s + sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), mx = s + sum_{i in F} max(0,w_i). A linear form over the subcube attains its min and max at vertices, so over the subcube min = mn and max = mx. If mn >= t, g is constantly 1; if mx < t, g is constantly 0. Hence non-constant implies mn < t <= mx, and the integers t with mn < t <= mx number mx - mn = W_F := sum_{i in F}|w_i|. Since t is uniform on 2R+1 >= W+1 integers, P_t(nonconst | F,a) <= W_F/(W+1). Taking expectation, E[W_F] = p W, so the probability is at most p W/(W+1) < p. Conversely, if mn < t <= mx then both constant values are attained, so the events coincide. QED. Consequence: for m gates with independent uniform thresholds, E[#nonconstant gates] <= p sum_j W_j/(W_j+1) <= p m, by linearity.

proved_step: CLAIMED LEMMA (+-1 weights, single THR gate, hand proof). Let w in {-1,0,1}^n have s >= 1 nonzero entries, t in Z fixed, F a random free set (each variable free independently with prob p), and a_i uniform in {0,1} on the non-free nonzero variables. Then P(gate non-constant after restriction) <= sqrt(2s) * p. Proof: (1) Given F, with k = |F cap supp(w)|, m = s - k, the gate is non-constant iff c in [t - kp, t + kn - 1], where kp, kn are the free positive and negative counts; this window has exactly k integers, because the free sum ranges over the contiguous set [-kn, kp] in unit steps. Here c is the fixed contribution. (2) With a uniform on the m non-free nonzero variables, c + m_- ~ Bin(m, 1/2), so max_x P(c = x) = C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m <= 1/sqrt(m) for m >= 1. Hence P(nonconst | F) <= min(1, k/sqrt(s-k)). (3) For k <= s/2, k/sqrt(s-k) <= sqrt2 k/sqrt s. For k > s/2 (s >= 2), sqrt2 k/sqrt s > sqrt(s/2) >= 1, so min(1, .) <= sqrt2 k/sqrt s. This also covers k = s (m = 0). (4) E[k] = sp, so P(nonconst) <= sqrt2 sp/sqrt s = sqrt(2s) p. The case s = 1 is trivial (P <= p). Equivalence: since free-sum steps are unit, nonconstancy is exactly the window event, so the statement is about non-constancy itself.

proved_step: CLAIMED LEMMA (bounded integer weights, single THR gate; generalises the +-1 lemma S0072 with B = 1). Setting: w in Z^n with s nonzero entries, |w_i| <= B for all i, t in Z fixed. F = free set, each variable free independently with prob p; each non-free nonzero variable gets a_i uniform in {0,1}. Claim: P(gate non-constant after restriction) <= B sqrt(2s) p for s >= 1. Proof. (1) Let k = |F cap supp(w)|, m = s - k, c = sum over non-free i of w_i a_i, X = sum over free i of w_i x_i. Non-constancy is min(c+X) < t <= max(c+X), i.e. c lies in a set of exactly max X - min X = W_F := sum_{i in F}|w_i| consecutive integers. (2) Erdos/Sperner: flip a_i to 1 - a_i where w_i < 0 (uniformity preserved), so c = (sum |w_i| a'_i) - const with |w_i| >= 1. For any half-open interval [y, y+1), the subset sums lying in it form an antichain (if A is a proper subset of B, the sums differ by >= 1), so there are at most C(m, floor(m/2)) of them. Hence max_x P(c = x) <= C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m <= 1/sqrt(m) for m >= 1. (3) So P(nonconst | F) <= min(1, W_F/sqrt(m)). (4) W_F <= B k. If k <= s/2 then m >= s/2 and B k/sqrt(m) <= sqrt2 B k/sqrt(s). If k > s/2 and s >= 2 then sqrt2 B k/sqrt(s) > B sqrt(s/2) >= 1, so the min is at most sqrt2 B k/sqrt(s). If s = 1, P(nonconst) <= P(k=1) = p <= sqrt2 B p. (5) E[k] = s p, so P(nonconst) <= sqrt2 B s p/sqrt(s) = B sqrt(2s) p. Corollary: with p = q/n and s <= n, the bound is B sqrt2 q/sqrt(n), the k/sqrt(n) shape of G0001 (per gate, in expectation, bounded weights only). proved_step: CLAIMED S-R26-LEMMA-UNIT-FIXED-THRESHOLD. Proof: fix F, k = |F|, m = n - k. Put s = sum_{i notin F} w_i a_i and mn = s + sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), mx = s + sum_{i in F} max(0,w_i). The subcube minimum and maximum of w.x are mn and mx, so non-constancy is equivalent to mn < t <= mx, i.e. s lies in a set I_F of exactly mx - mn = k integers (all |w_i| = 1). (1) Distribution of s given F: s = sum_{w_i=+1} a_i + sum_{w_i=-1} (1-a_i) - N_- where N_- = #{i notin F: w_i=-1}; the terms a_i and 1-a_i are i.i.d. uniform bits, so s is a fixed integer shift of Bin(m,1/2). Hence each point probability is at most C(m,floor(m/2))/2^m <= sqrt(2/(pi m)) (standard central binomial bound, valid for all m >= 1). Therefore P_a(nonconst | F) <= min(1, k sqrt(2/(pi m))). (2) Case k <= n/2: then m >= n/2 >= 1/2, so sqrt(2/(pi m)) <= 2/sqrt(pi n) < sqrt(2/n), giving P_a(nonconst|F) <= k sqrt(2/n). Taking expectation, E[k 1(k<=n/2)] <= E[k] = pn, so this part contributes at most p sqrt(2n). (3) Case k > n/2: bound the conditional probability by 1; by Markov, P(k >= n/2) <= E[k]/(n/2) = 2p. Adding: P <= p sqrt(2n) + 2p. QED. Consequence: for m' gates with the same (F,a) law, E[#nonconstant gates] <= m' p(sqrt(2n)+2), by linearity, with no independence needed.

lemma: Few-distinct-rows subclass (O2). Let n>=1, B>=1, and let W in Z^{m x n} have all entries in [-B,B] and at most r distinct rows, with distinct row set F = {F_1..F_r} (F_f in Z^n), row map sigma: [m] -> [r], thresholds t in Z^m, weights v in Z^m, T in Z. Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n. Then #SAT(f) = sum over s in S of c(s) g(s), where S = {(F_f.x)_f : x in {0,1}^n}, c(s) = #{x : (F_f.x)_f = s}, g(s) = [sum_j v_j [s_{sigma(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. The DP over coordinates i = 1..n (c_{i+1}(s) = c_i(s) + c_i(s - F_{.,i+1})) computes c exactly, since the value vector after i coordinates depends only on x_1..x_i. Every coordinate of s lies in [-Bn, Bn], so |S| <= (2Bn+1)^r. Time: O((nr + m)(2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations, times a log factor for hashing. Hence for fixed r and B the count is poly(n, m). Corollary: if r*log2(2Bn+1) <= n/2 the time is 2^(n/2) * poly(n,m), a saving over brute force 2^n * m on this subclass.

lemma: Uniform-threshold restriction identity. Let W in Z^{1 x n} with S_+ = sum_j max(W_j,0), S_- = sum_j min(W_j,0), S = S_+ - S_- = sum_j |W_j|, lo = S_-, hi = S_+. Let t be uniform on the S+1 integers {lo,...,hi}. Fix x in {0,1}^n and a free set F. Let const = sum_{j not in F} W_j x_j, flo = const + sum_{j in F} min(W_j,0), fhi = const + sum_{j in F} max(W_j,0). The gate is undecided under the restriction iff flo < t <= fhi. Then P_t[undecided] = W_F/(S+1) exactly, where W_F = sum_{j in F}|W_j|. Averaging over a uniformly random free set F of size k: E_F[P_t[undecided]] = (k/n) S/(S+1) <= k/n.
